moat_against: Low measured returns through the cycle: ROE 1.7% (2023), 3.0% (2024), -5.6% (2025); no computable ROIC series (operating income untagged)
Continuing-basis gross margin only 32.8% / 33.0% / 34.5% (2023-25) — pricing power is real but bounded
PFAS legacy liabilities — NJ settlement share ~$177M present value over 25 years, NC settlement cost-sharing, and open matters: a multi-decade cash drag
Cyclical end markets in Diversified Industrials: construction, automotive, printing & packaging
Portfolio still shrinking: Aramids (Kevlar/Nomex) sold April 2026 after the Qnity spin — smaller, less diversified base
moat_for: Tyvek leadership in medical packaging and construction envelopes — spec-in, qualification-locked positions
FilmTec reverse-osmosis membranes — leading position in water treatment with installed-base replacement demand
Healthcare & Water Technologies operating EBITDA margin 30.1% in Q2 2026 (company release)
Patent and brand portfolio plus regulatory qualifications raise customer switching costs
moat_justification: Market-leading, spec-in franchises (Tyvek, FilmTec membranes) with qualification switching costs and a 30.1% Q2 2026 operating EBITDA margin in Healthcare & Water, but measured returns on capital are low through the cycle (ROE 1.7% in 2023, 3.0% in 2024, -5.6% in 2025 on the filed history; roic_proxy not computable because operating income is untagged) and continuing-basis gross margin is only 32.8-34.5% — a narrow/moderate moat, not a wide one.
name: DuPont de Nemours, Inc.
one_liner: Solid specialty-materials franchise, moat 5/10 — on TTM owner's earnings of $4.80/share the weighted IRR is 6.6% at $132.70 (weighted IV@15% $42.35); it clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$42 — the post-reverse-split price capitalizes an adjusted-EPS recovery that cash owner's earnings do not yet support.
